name: The Lantern Court
site: A court annex off the falls that is only in session where lanterns have been set down. It is not City Hall. It convenes in the gap the city did not measure.
premise: Shadows copy what Ellis just did. The copy is written on a testimony rail as verb and direction, eight beats visible, newest last. An exemplar performs the legal sequence in the room, and the same sequence is cut into stone or wood there. A clerk's bell rewinds the copy without taking keys. The Second Crown is resolved here as a proposed integration event. It does not grant Embryonic God.

input.keyboard: cardinal movement and a single action
input.touch: cardinal pad and tap on the interaction tile
input.parity: WAIT, PLACE, and RING are tiles, not keyboard-only chords.

campaignPrerequisites.note: Placed light uses the lamp plus spare court lanterns that never leave the room.

proposedUnlocks.note: Resolves crown 2, the Lantern Crown. Eligibility for Embryonic God is a contribution recorded in integration/second-crown.event.json. This pack does not set that eligibility.

death.epitaph: In {roomName}, the body stopped. Ellis Perch drew the next breath fourteen years on. The rail of that attempt is blank. The docket is not.
death.voiceOnReentry: The court finally kept a face for the unmeasured life. You did not lend it yours.
death.otherVoiceOnReentry: The court kept a record of a refusal. Do not let the office call the refusal a birth.

shortcut.description: After the playable record is latched, a service corridor joins the docket hall to the crown threshold. A later body skips the middle court.

clues.text: An exemplar shadow loops north, north, east, ring. It repeats until Ellis matches it or rings the bell.
The same four beats are inlaid in the floor in slate: N, N, E, a bell-cut.
The exemplar plays north, east, east, north, ring, and then plays it again.
The wall carving is the same five beats. The testimony rail shows Ellis's beats beside it, mismatch in red wax.
Arrows cut in Ellis's rail read north, north, south. The shadow's next tile is chalked before it moves.
The exemplar walks that arrow order on the far rail, forever, including the plates lighting as it goes.

evidence.name: The Town vs. The Unmeasured Life
evidence.text: Docket heading cut into the bench. The charge is that a life resumed in Addison County without a new birth, and that the office would like this called a zero.

evidence.name: The two voices on one event
evidence.text: Voice, left bench: The vein kept Ellis because a crown must be worn by a continued life. Other Voice, right bench: A continued life is a person. A crown is the court admitting it failed to file the person. They are answering the same docket line and do not agree.

evidence.name: Scrap under the bench
evidence.text: A juror's scrap: we copied the steps we were shown. When the copy went wrong the bell put us back at the start of the steps, not at the start of our lives.

evidence.name: Exhibit card
evidence.text: The card inside the cage, repeating the docket so it does not have to be remembered: nail, page, lantern. The bases of the three objects are stamped with those words.

evidence.name: The playable record
evidence.text: The floor keeps Ellis's successful five beats as a record that can be walked again. It is evidence because it was done, not because it was written about. The Second Crown proposal requires this record alongside the adjournment.

evidence.name: Scraped years
evidence.text: Portraits with the faces planed off. The lamp finds years, not mouths: 1849, 1863, 1877, and onward by fourteens. Optional. The court does not require Ellis to count them.

evidence.name: Adjournment
evidence.text: The witness without a face bows. The record states that Ellis stood where a face was asked for and set down a light instead. Crown two is marked resolved. No god is declared.

enemies.name: Shade clerk
enemies.telegraph: An afterimage flickers on the tile the clerk will step to, one beat later, copying Ellis's last cardinal step.

rooms.name: The Witness Without a Face
rooms.summary: Boss. An empty face asks to be worn. Ellis places lanterns where the exemplar places them, reads the chalk copy before each lunge, and sets the lamp on the center stand instead of offering a face. The bell clears a bad copy and keeps the hit count already landed. Adjournment resolves the Second Crown as a proposal.
solutionTrace: Place lanterns left, right, and bench as the exemplar does. Strike the solid shadow three times.
Read the chalk. Step aside. Strike three times on the recovery. Ring the bell if the copy is garbage; the strikes already landed stay.
Set the lamp on the center stand. Strike four times. The crown event is proposed at adjournment, not before.

mirror.note: A banner over the aisle shows the direction the bailiff will copy next: Ellis's previous step. WAIT is a legal step.

stalled.tell: The banner reads WAIT. The bailiff copies it and does not move.

b_h0.note: The bailiff copied WAIT and stalled.

call_to_order.note: The docket board lights with the phase order and stays lit. South door stays open.

phase1_place.tell: An exemplar shadow places lanterns left, right, then bench, once, in view.

phase2_copy.tell: The witness stores three steps. Before any lunge, chalk draws those steps on the floor.

phase2_lunge.tell: The lunge follows the chalk and not a hidden buffer.

phase3_mask.tell: A mask walks. The docket line reads: the face is the light you put down.

adjourned.note: The witness bows to an empty bench. This is the proposed Second Crown resolution, not a costume and not Embryonic God by itself.

p1_h0.note: The witness's shadow is solid where the lanterns agree with the docket.

p2_h0.note: The lunge missed. The chalked copy is still on the floor.

p3_h0.note: The mask burns on the center stand. The face does not arrive.
